html:
The Indigenous practice of growing maize, beans and squash together in one field, the base of farming across much of North America by about 1000 to 1300.

Each plant helps the others:

  • Maize gives a tall stalk for the beans to climb.
  • Beans add nitrogen to the soil.
  • Squash spreads its broad leaves over the ground, which keeps weeds down and holds moisture.

Together they also make a balanced diet, since beans supply what maize lacks. All three came from Mexico, where the same mix is grown in the milpa field, and spread north over many centuries. They largely replaced the older seed crops of the Eastern Agricultural Complex.

The name comes from the Haudenosaunee, whose stories tell of three sisters who belong together. The crops fed the towns of Cahokia and the villages of the Northeast, and later the first English settlers, who learned the method from their neighbours.
sum: The Indigenous practice of growing maize, beans and squash together in one field, the base of farming across much of North America by about 1000 to 1300.
